meta.what: Instructions in each generated serialise and deserialise entry point of the host-image fixtures, read off llvm-objdump for the object target on a pinned triple.
meta.why_this_unit: A static count of a function's instructions is a property of the emitted code: exact, host-independent, and readable without a simulator, so it gates where the cachegrind lanes skip. The fold's worth was first measured this way, by hand.
meta.keys: counts[llvm-<major>][<triple>][<symbol>]. The count moves when the compiler moves, so the LLVM major is part of the key; a key with no entry skips and prints the values to paste. Re-baseline in the commit that changes the lowering.
meta.control: Padded is not a host image and does not fold; its counts pin the field-wise body beside the folded ones.

measured.llvm-22: LLVM 22.1.8, 2026-09-30, a host-image deserialise folds every nested record's code

meta.accessors: The field accessors of phase 4 are baselined beside the bodies: a getter, a setter, an element getter and a composite getter. A whole-function count includes the cold path: a getter's hot path is a bounds check and one load on a little-endian target, and the primitive it keeps for a buffer short of the field is the rest of the count.
meta.views: A container holding a view of an @aliasable record, under --aliasable-views (`views:`) and as a decoded copy (`plain:`). A static count is per function, and the plain path's nested decode is a call, so the holder's own count does not show what the view removes: that is the callee, baselined beside it under `plain:`.
